post.caption:
Commercial bananas are seedless, so they cannot breed. Every Cavendish on Earth is a cutting from the same plant, genetically one individual. Monoculture like that means zero variation, so a pathogen that beats one plant beats all of them. It has already happened once: Gros Michel was wiped out by Panama disease in the 1950s. Cavendish replaced it because it resisted that strain, and a new strain is now moving through it.
